text:
noah: quick PSA — after the kernel-selector change rolled yesterday we're seeing a regression in PP 1F1B latency for long sequences (seq=2048). p50 up ~12% and tail worse. Seen on both dedicated and local dev rigs. anyone else?

sasha: saw it on the nightly cluster run at 03:10 UTC. thought it was noise but the profile says otherwise. attaching summary below.

bench-bot: nightly/pp-1f1b/17642: summary -> microbatch=4, pp=8, tp=2, precision=fp16, seq=2048:
- mean token latency: 163ms (baseline was 145ms)
- p50: 150ms -> 168ms
- p95: 240ms -> 285ms
- all-reduce time ratio increased from 9% -> 18% overall
- average queued kernels per step: increased from 2.1 -> 4.6
- note: fused-attn kernel usage dropped 78% -> 6% (kernel-selector picked split attention)

maria: interesting — kernel-selector change was intentional to improve quantized accuracy for the new llama-variants. but we didn't gate it by schedule type (1F1B vs fill-and-drain). looks like split-attn has more launches and smaller kernel occupancy which hurts comm overlap.

aj: can you paste the profiler flame? even a small snippet helps.

sasha: pasted profiler excerpt (torch profiler + nsight sampling):
```
Step 1234 timeline (simplified):
[compute-kernel A]  0 - 1.6ms
[compute-kernel B]  1.6 - 2.9ms
[ncclAllReduce]     2.9 - 6.8ms  <-- increased latency and blocking
[enqueue memcpy]   6.8 - 7.0ms
[compute-kernel C]  7.0 - 8.1ms
[ncclAllReduce]     8.1 - 12.0ms

Old timeline (fused-attn):
[compute-kernel F]  0 - 3.4ms  (fewer launches, higher occupancy)
[ncclAllReduce]     3.4 - 5.0ms  (overlapped better)
```

sasha: takeaway: split kernels double the number of kernel launches per layer. with microbatch=4 on 1F1B we don't have enough independent compute to hide the second all-reduce. net effect: more serialization.

noah: gutsy. so two knobs: increase microbatch to give more ops to overlap OR change kernel selector to prefer fused variants when schedule==1F1B. also consider batching heuristics to coalesce small tensors before all-reduce.

maria: I ran a quick sweep on dev box (pp=4, tp=1):
- microbatch=2 -> p50 180ms
- microbatch=4 -> p50 168ms (current)
- microbatch=8 -> p50 155ms (closer to baseline)
So increasing microbatch helps but it's not free (memory + latency tradeoff).

aj: what about comm fusion? we have an experimental "allreduce-fuse" switch that groups small tensors into 1 NCCL op. bench-bot had a run earlier: enabling fuse decreased all-reduce ratio 18% -> 11% and p50 returned to ~148ms.

bench-bot: run id 176420-fuse: microbatch=4, fuse=on -> mean token latency 150ms, p95 260ms.

noah: perfect. sounds like short-term mitigation: enable allreduce-fuse in runtime for schedules that have high kernel-launch counts. medium-term: kernel-selector should be schedule-aware (or expose policy override). long-term: consider a scheduler that can dynamically choose microbatch per workload to match comm/compute balance.

maria: one more wrinkle — KV cache memcpy pattern changed too. split-attn path emits more small KV updates, increasing device->device memcpy freq which punctuates compute windows and prevents overlap. profiler shows extra small copies at layer boundaries.

aj: yeah I saw that: NVTX shows repeated memcpy launches every layer. We should add a coalescing pass for KV updates (coalesce per-stage). I can prototype a patch to buffer KV writes per microbatch and flush once per stage.

sasha: proposal and action items:
1) short-term (today): enable allreduce-fuse for 1F1B schedules on warm clusters (maria).
2) short-term (today): bump default microbatch to 8 for sequences >=1024 on pp>=4 (ops experiment, no config change for hosted yet) (noah).
3) med-term (week): add schedule-aware kernel-policy in selector (sasha + maria) — prefer fused kernels when they improve comm overlap for 1F1B.
4) med-term (week): KV coalescing pass prototype (aj).
5) infra: run full nightly heatmap sweep with microbatch in {2,4,8,12} and fuse on/off, collect flame + nccl traces (bench-bot + infra-bot).

infra-bot: created perf-issue #4567 and scheduled nightly sweep job: https://perf.internal/redwood/pp-1f1b/heatmap/17642

noah: thanks all. let's try the microbatch bump + fuse and re-run the failing canary. ping here with results. :thumbsup:
